findings.issue_text: [BUG] The PR only wraps scale-color in dark-light-choose, but this line silently changes the light-theme value from $lightness: 30% to $lightness: 70%. In light themes the reply-by/quoted-user link renders at primary lightened 70% instead of 30% — a near-invisible pale color where a dark bold link used to be; this is a visual regression inconsistent with the PR's stated wrap-only intent.

[BUG] The .name color value changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to $lightness: 50% under the guise of the dark-light-choose wrap. In light themes the user-profile name is rendered 20% lighter than before; adjacent .title keeps its original 50%, so the two now render identically, erasing the intended hierarchy between name and title.

[BUG] The mobile .name color value changed from $lightness: 30% to $lightness: 50% in the same hunk that adds dark-light-choose. Light-theme mobile users see the profile name washed out relative to the previous 30% value, and it now matches .title exactly, losing the deliberate contrast the old values encoded.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length color changed from $lightness: 70% to $lightness: 30% while wrapping, the opposite direction of a pure wrap. In light themes the character-count hint in the flag/message modal becomes much darker than before (30% instead of 70% lightness), visually overweighting what was designed as a faint hint text.

[BUG] The suggestion h3 color changed from $lightness: 20% to $lightness: 50% in the same edit that adds dark-light-choose. Light-theme mobile suggested-topic headings drop from a near-primary 20% to a mid-gray 50%, visibly lighter than the desktop equivalent (which correctly keeps 20% at desktop/topic-post.scss line ~321), producing a cross-form inconsistency.

[BUG] The category-topic-link figure color changed from $lightness: 10% to $lightness: 90% in the same edit that adds dark-light-choose. In light themes the bold numeric glyph flips from almost fully saturated primary (10%) to an extremely pale 90% wash, making the count effectively unreadable against a white background — a near-total contrast loss on mobile category pages.

[BUG] The light-mode value for .custom-message-length was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) — the 70/30 pair was written inverted (30/70) instead of preserving the original 70% light value. In light themes, the custom-message-length hint text in the mobile modal renders much darker (30% lightness primary instead of 70%), an unintended visual regression in a PR that claims to only change dark-theme rendering.

[BUG] The light-mode value for .names a was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) — the original 30% was misplaced into the dark (secondary) slot, producing a 70/30 pair instead of 30/70. In light themes, the poster name link in embedded reply previews renders near-background (70% lightness) instead of the intended strong 30% lightness, making it nearly unreadable — a light-mode regression introduced by a dark-theme-only PR.

[BUG] The light-mode value for .name was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), collapsing the name/title color hierarchy (the adjacent .title at line 525 is also 50%). In light themes, the user's display name on the user card loses its intended stronger contrast (30% lightness) and now renders identically to the .title below it, flattening the visual hierarchy the 30% value existed to provide.

[BUG] The light-mode value for .name was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), the same drift as desktop/user.scss (adjacent .title at line 500 is also 50%). In light themes on mobile, the user card display name renders at 50% lightness instead of 30%, matching .title instead of standing out — an unintended light-mode visual regression.

[BUG] The light-mode value for the link h3 was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) — the strongest heading color in this block was weakened to match h4. In light themes, the link preview h3 heading renders at 50% lightness instead of the intended 20%, losing its deliberate emphasis over the 50%-lightness h4/domain text below it — a light-mode regression in a dark-theme-only PR.

[ADVISORY] The sibling dark-theme color function on the same path, .wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }, was left unconverted while the adjacent disabled-state colors in the same hunk were wrapped in dark-light-choose. In dark themes the composer editor text uses darken($primary, 40%) — since $primary is light in dark schemas, darkening it 40% yields dark gray text on a dark editor background, giving poor contrast exactly in the input the diff was converting around; a future conversion pass will also have to revisit this file.

[ADVISORY] A hard-coded background-color: white remains in .invalid .hex input, in the same selector block whose sibling (.description) was converted for dark themes in this diff. In dark themes, the invalid hex-color input in the badge admin screen keeps a hard white background while surrounding text/borders are theme-aware, producing a jarring bright patch admins see on every validation error; it will need a separate dark-theme fix since this PR was the pass over this file.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was silently changed from 30% to 70%: the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)` — the dark branch got the mirror of the wrong number. In light themes this username link renders much lighter (lightness 70% instead of 30%), a visible regression unrelated to the PR's stated dark-theme intent; every theme that uses a light scheme changes appearance with no requirement covering it.

[BUG] The light/dark branches are swapped relative to the original value and to the desktop twin: original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` becomes light-branch 30% / dark-branch 70%, while desktop/modal.scss's identical `.custom-message-length` rule keeps light 70% / dark 30%. Mobile light-theme modals render the hint at lightness 30% (nearly full-strength text instead of a dim hint), and mobile dark theme gets `scale-color($secondary, 70%)` which does not match the mirroring convention (100−N) used everywhere else in this diff; the same class renders differently on desktop and mobile.

[BUG] The light-theme value was changed from 20% to 50% (`scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` became light branch 50%), diverging from the desktop counterpart in desktop/topic-post.scss line ~319 which correctly keeps light 20% / dark 80%. Mobile light themes render the search-result h3 at half-dim instead of near-full strength — a light-theme visual regression not traceable to the 'dark themes' requirement, plus a desktop/mobile inconsistency for the same component.

[BUG] The light-theme branch value was changed from 30% to 50%: original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, while the adjacent `.title` rule correctly keeps its original 50%. Light-theme user profile names render dimmer than before (50% instead of 30%), reducing contrast against the 50% title next to it — an unrequested light-theme change bundled into a dark-theme PR.

[BUG] Same drifted value as desktop: original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` becomes light branch 50%, changing the light-theme rendering of the mobile profile name. Mobile light-theme usernames render at 50% lightness instead of 30%, a regression with no requirement behind it; both the desktop and mobile `.name` rules were silently altered while the neighboring `.title` rules kept their values, confirming the drift is accidental.

[ADVISORY] The adjacent `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` inside the same hunk range is left scheme-unaware, the same class of defect the PR states it is eliminating (`darken` produces an absolute dark color regardless of scheme). In dark themes the composer input text is a mid-gray derived by darkening an already-light primary, dimming editor text on a dark background while the surrounding disabled-input colors in the same block were made theme-aware — an inconsistency operators will report as 'composer text too faint in dark mode'.

[ADVISORY] The hand-maintained paired-enumeration pattern `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-X%))` is repeated ~60 times across 24 files with no shared mixin or function, and this diff itself demonstrates the failure mode: five sites got mismatched or swapped pairs. Every future color touch requires a human to keep two numbers and their mirror relationship in sync across light and dark branches; this PR already shipped five broken pairs (desktop/topic-post.scss 291, mobile/modal.scss 102, mobile/topic-post.scss 182, desktop/user.scss 522, mobile/user.scss 498), and the next batch of conversions will repeat the mistake because nothing in the code encodes the invariant the PR title states.

[ADVISORY] The stated invariant ('scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes') is only enforced for the subset of sites converted in this diff; unconverted `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` occurrences remain elsewhere in admin_base.scss and other stylesheets, so nothing (lint rule, mixin, or test) prevents the pattern from being reintroduced. Dark-theme users continue to see primary-derived colors that wash out or vanish on dark backgrounds at every site this PR did not reach, and new code can freely add bare `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` again since no guard enforces the rule the PR title declares.

[BUG] In the `.replies a` rule the light-theme value was flipped along with the dark one: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)` — the light path silently changed from 30% to 70% instead of being preserved. Users on light color schemes see the reply-to author names in .replies rendered in a much fainter color (70% lightness vs the previous 30%) — a light-theme visual regression shipped by a PR whose scope is dark themes only, caused by mechanically applying the (100−L) mirror to the first argument too.

[BUG] The `.profile .name` rule changed its light-theme value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, altering light-theme rendering instead of only adding a dark variant. On light color schemes the user profile display name loses its emphasis relative to adjacent elements (it was styled at 30% like `.username a` two hunks up, which the diff correctly kept at 30/70); it now renders at the same faded 50% as `.title`, a visible regression outside the PR's stated scope.

[BUG] `.custom-message-length` changed its light-theme value from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), ...)` — the mirror flip was applied to the light argument, inverting the intended contrast. On mobile light themes the remaining-characters counter under the composer jumps from a faint 70%-lightness hint color to a much darker 30% color, visually promoting a secondary hint to near-primary text weight; the desktop counterpart of this exact rule (desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length, changed in this same diff to 70/30) now disagrees with mobile.

[BUG] The shared/referred-post `h3` heading changed its light-theme value from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)` — 20% was not preserved, and 50% is not even the mirror of 20% (80% would be). On mobile light themes the linked-topic title in the quote/share preview drops from strong 20%-lightness text to the same faded 50% as its `h4` subtitle below it, collapsing the visual hierarchy between title and subtitle; the desktop twin of this rule (desktop/topic-post.scss h3, correctly changed to 20/80 in this diff) now diverges from mobile.

[BUG] The mobile `.profile .name` rule changed its light-theme value from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)` — the light argument was flipped along with the dark one. On mobile light themes the profile display name renders at faded 50% instead of its previous 30%, silently matching the desktop bug at desktop/user.scss:519-523 in this same diff so both profile-name sites regress identically and are easy to miss as a pair.

[ADVISORY] The diff hand-computes the dark-theme mirror value (100−L)% for roughly 90 call sites instead of extracting a SCSS function/mixin that derives the dark variant from the light lightness, and the manual arithmetic has already produced five wrong values in this very diff (desktop/topic-post.scss .replies a, desktop/user.scss .name, mobile/modal.scss .custom-message-length, mobile/topic-post.scss h3, mobile/user.scss .name). Every future theme-contrast sweep repeats this error-prone manual mirror across dozens of files; a `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l))` helper would make the invariant structural and would have made the five slips in this diff impossible or at least diff-visible as a single call-site change.

[BUG] The mechanical dark-mode rewrite silently changed the light-theme value here: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, flipping the light-branch lightness from 30% to 70% instead of preserving it and adding a 70%-secondary dark branch. Every user on a light theme sees this bold link (in the small-action/reply summary block) rendered at 70% lightness instead of 30% — a dramatically dimmer color that no reviewer or accepter of the PR's stated intent ('must use $secondary for dark themes') signed off on; the dark branch also gets 30%-secondary where the diff's own consistent scheme (primary X% pairs with secondary (100-X)%) calls for 70%.

[BUG] The `.name` selector's light-theme color was silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` inside the new dark-light-choose call, instead of preserving the light value and only adding a dark branch. Light-theme users see the user profile name rendered dimmer (50% vs 30% lightness) than the accepted design; the sibling common/base/user.scss `.name` rule in this same diff correctly preserves 30% for light and adds 70% for dark, proving this site is drift, not intent.

[BUG] The mobile `.name` selector's light-theme color was silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, the same drift as its desktop counterpart, instead of preserving the light value. Mobile light-theme users see the profile name dimmer than the accepted design, and inconsistently with the common/base/user.scss `.name` rule (30% light / 70% dark) that this same diff established.

[BUG] `.custom-message-length` had its light-theme value silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, and its dark branch set to 70%-secondary — both branches flipped relative to the desktop counterpart in desktop/modal.scss (70% primary light / 30% secondary dark). Light-theme mobile users see the custom-message-length hint rendered far darker (30% vs 70% lightness) than the accepted design, and the same hint renders differently on mobile vs desktop in both themes, an inconsistency introduced without any stated change of objective.

[BUG] The suggested-topic `h3` light-theme color was silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, instead of preserving 20% for light and adding 80%-secondary for dark as the desktop version in desktop/topic-post.scss (line ~318) correctly did. Mobile light-theme users see suggested-topic headings rendered noticeably dimmer (50% vs 20% lightness) than the accepted design, and inconsistently with the same heading on desktop, a divergence the PR title ('must use $secondary for dark themes') never proposed.

[BUG] The mechanical dark-light-choose substitution at `.title a` swapped the operands: the original light-theme value `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, silently changing the light-theme color from 30% to 70% lightness instead of preserving it and pairing it with secondary 70%. Light-theme users see this quote-title link rendered as a very faint (primary lightened 70%) color where it was previously a much darker 30%-lightness color — an unrequested visual regression on a path this PR never intended to touch; every other site in this diff preserves the original light value.

[BUG] The mobile `h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(...50%..., ...50%...)`, silently changing the light-theme value from 20% to 50% lightness even though the identical desktop selector in desktop/topic-post.scss was correctly converted to primary-20%/secondary-80%. Mobile light-theme users get a washed-out section heading (50% lightness) that no longer matches the desktop rendering of the same component (20%/80%), diverging solely because of an inconsistent mechanical substitution; the light theme's appearance changes with no test or screenshot covering it.

[BUG] The mobile `.custom-message-length` color was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, inverting the original light-theme value (primary lightened 70%), while the same selector in desktop/modal.scss (line 94) was correctly converted preserving light 70% with secondary 30%. Light-theme mobile users see this hint text rendered much darker (primary lightened 30%) than before and than the desktop rendering of the identical class, a silent light-theme regression caused by swapped operands in the mechanical refactor.

[BUG] The desktop user-profile `.name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently altering the light-theme value from 30% to 50% lightness, out of scope for a PR whose stated change is only about dark themes. Light-theme users see the user's display name rendered noticeably lighter than before on the profile header, an unintended visual change smuggled into a mechanical dark-theme refactor with no screenshot or test to catch it.

[BUG] The mobile user-profile `.name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently altering the light-theme value from 30% to 50% lightness, mirroring the same out-of-scope drift as desktop/user.scss line 522. Light-theme mobile users see the profile display name rendered lighter than the pre-PR value on an unchanged code path, an unintended visual regression introduced by the bulk substitution rather than by design.
